sources.entry: Puter - Web-based operating system designed to be feature-rich, exceptionally fast, and highly extensible. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: Puter is an open-source, self-hostable "internet computer": a web-based operating system with built-in apps, cloud storage, and developer tools for building and publishing web apps.
summary.what_it_does: Puter runs as a desktop-style operating system in the browser, bundling apps such as a Notepad, Voice Recorder, Spreadsheet, and Camera. For developers, the README says it provides AI, cloud storage, a database, and serverless workers for building web apps and games, and that apps can be published to its App Store. It can be run locally with npm install and npm start, built and run with Docker via a local docker-compose.override.yml, or self-hosted with a one-line install script for Linux/macOS or a PowerShell command for Windows. A hosted version is available at puter.com.
use_cases: build and publish web apps or games
run a browser-based office and productivity environment
host cloud storage and a database for web apps
try an internet-based OS without installing software
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
For self-hosting: curl -fsSL <install script URL> | sh (Linux/macOS) or irm <install script URL> | iex (Windows); see Self-Hosting Puter in the docs
notable: Browser-based operating system with built-in apps such as Notepad, Voice Recorder, Spreadsheet, and Camera
Developer platform including AI, cloud storage, database, and serverless workers
App Store for publishing and distributing web apps
Can be run locally via npm or Docker, with one-line self-hosting install scripts
caveats: The README's install commands have blank URLs, so exact setup links must be taken from the full docs
Docker setup requires a local docker-compose.override.yml to select the local build
Monetization and reaching users are tied to its App Store, which is a hosted service element
